group.name: Cisco SD-WAN Receiver
group.description: Dashboard group for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager telemetry emitted by the Cisco OS receiver.

dashboards.name: 00 SD-WAN Fleet API And Manager Health
dashboards.description: First-response dashboard for SD-WAN Manager API trust, scrape completeness, inventory, and product coverage.
dashboards.value: Proves whether SD-WAN Manager polling is healthy before operators trust inventory, overlay, path, event, or feature-group panels.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to use the SD-WAN fleet dashboard as the incident starting point. Interpretation: start here when SD-WAN telemetry is missing, stale, partially successful, or when API/feature coverage may be hiding network state.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
Use this dashboard as the first Splunk Observability page for Catalyst SD-WAN incidents. It separates collection trust from WAN symptoms: API errors, rate limits, unavailable feature groups, skipped target-scoped groups, partial scrapes, and stale timestamps explain visibility gaps before operators trust overlay or app-path evidence.

charts.name: SD-WAN Partial Scrape
charts.description: Value: proves whether one or more SD-WAN endpoint families failed or were skipped during collection. Interpretation: 1 means the dashboard may be incomplete and should be read alongside API and service coverage charts.

charts.name: API Request Errors
charts.description: Value: surfaces failed SD-WAN Manager API calls by operation and HTTP status. Interpretation: non-zero values explain missing inventory, overlay, app-route, alarm, event, audit, or feature-group data.

charts.name: API Request Duration
charts.description: Value: detects slow SD-WAN Manager API operations. Interpretation: rising duration by operation can precede partial scrapes, stale dashboards, or delayed incident evidence.

charts.name: Feature Coverage Gaps
charts.description: Value: shows unavailable or skipped SD-WAN feature groups. Interpretation: unavailable means endpoint, license, role, permission, or version gap; skipped usually means an opt-in group needs target filters.

charts.name: Device Reachability
charts.description: Value: identifies SD-WAN devices reported reachable or unreachable. Interpretation: each row is a device; 1 means up or reachable and 0 means unavailable.

charts.name: API Rate Limits
charts.description: Value: surfaces the SD-WAN Manager API throttling rate by operation. Interpretation: non-zero values explain missing or delayed endpoint data even when authentication succeeds.

charts.name: Last Successful Scrape
charts.description: Value: shows the most recent successful SD-WAN scrape timestamp by manager. Interpretation: stale timestamps mean downstream dashboards may be showing old network state.

charts.name: Manager Availability And Status
charts.description: Value: shows whether SD-WAN Manager and exposed manager services are healthy. Interpretation: down or degraded rows mean collection and product state should be investigated before WAN symptoms.

charts.name: Manager Health And Inventory Scope
charts.description: Value: connects manager health score with selected inventory size. Interpretation: falling health or sudden inventory count changes indicate product, permission, or target-scope problems.

dashboards.name: 01 Control Plane Overlay And Validity
dashboards.description: Overlay health dashboard for SD-WAN device validity, certificates, control connections, and BFD sessions.
dashboards.value: Connects WAN Edge/controller validity, certificate state, control connections, and BFD session health into one overlay triage page.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how overlay symptoms are organized for SD-WAN incidents. Interpretation: use validity and certificate state first, then control connection and BFD state to decide whether the issue is lifecycle, controller reachability, or transport path health.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page connects SD-WAN resource status, device validity, certificate validity, control connections, expected versus actual control sessions, and BFD sessions. It helps determine whether application impact is caused by lifecycle/certificate state, controller connectivity, or tunnel/path health.

charts.name: Resource And Validity Status
charts.description: Value: shows encoded device/resource, validity, and certificate state. Interpretation: warning or error states explain path problems even when an interface appears up.

charts.name: Control Connection Status
charts.description: Value: shows SD-WAN control connection health by device, peer type, and color. Interpretation: down or degraded rows indicate controller/overlay control-plane loss.

charts.name: Control Expected Versus Actual
charts.description: Value: compares expected and actual control connections when exposed by SD-WAN Manager. Interpretation: actual below expected indicates missing controller sessions or partial overlay connectivity.

charts.name: BFD Session Status
charts.description: Value: shows tunnel/path health through BFD session state. Interpretation: partial or down BFD sessions can explain application impact even when control connections remain up.

charts.name: Control And BFD Session Counts
charts.description: Value: counts control and BFD sessions by state. Interpretation: falling healthy counts or rising degraded counts identify overlay scope and path loss faster than row-by-row status alone.

dashboards.name: 02 Site BFD TLOC Tunnel And Underlay Health
dashboards.description: Site, BFD, TLOC, tunnel, and underlay health dashboard for SD-WAN path triage.
dashboards.value: Shows BFD session state, TLOC color context, tunnel/underlay feature coverage, and path instability evidence for affected sites.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to use BFD, TLOC, tunnel, and underlay evidence for SD-WAN incidents. Interpretation: use this page when a site or transport color is suspected and compare session state with feature coverage gaps.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
Use this page to isolate SD-WAN path health by site, system IP, local color, remote color, and remote system IP. BFD status and transition counts show tunnel stability; opt-in tunnel and underlay groups surface product coverage or endpoint gaps when those modules are enabled.

charts.name: BFD Session Status By Site And Color
charts.description: Value: shows BFD tunnel/path state by device, site, color, and remote peer. Interpretation: down or degraded rows indicate transport path loss even if SD-WAN control plane remains up.

charts.name: BFD Transitions And Flaps
charts.description: Value: shows BFD transition and flap rates. Interpretation: rising transition or flap rates during the incident window indicate unstable circuits, provider paths, or transport colors.

charts.name: Tunnel And Underlay Coverage
charts.description: Value: shows whether opt-in tunnel and underlay feature groups are producing data or reporting gaps. Interpretation: unavailable endpoints usually mean feature, license, role, version, or permission gaps rather than clean tunnel health.
charts.signalflow: data('sdwan.collection.object.count', filter=filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'tunnels')).sum(by=['sdwan.collection.group', 'sdwan.collection.operation']).publish(label='Tunnel objects'); data('sdwan.collection.object.count', filter=filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'underlay')).sum(by=['sdwan.collection.group', 'sdwan.collection.operation']).publish(label='Underlay objects'); data('sdwan.service.unavailable', filter=filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'tunnels') or filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'underlay')).sum(by=['sdwan.collection.group', 'sdwan.collection.operation']).publish(label='Unavailable')

dashboards.name: 03 Application Experience SaaS And AI Paths
dashboards.description: Application and AI path dashboard for app-route loss, latency, jitter, SLA state, and transport color selection.
dashboards.value: Focuses on app-route loss, latency, jitter, SLA state, local/remote colors, and AI/model/SaaS application filters.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to troubleshoot application, SaaS, and AI/model paths. Interpretation: compare app-route latency, jitter, loss, and SLA state by application and color before looking at policy, security, Cloud OnRamp, or data-center fabric evidence.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page focuses on SD-WAN application experience, including model/API endpoints, SaaS AI assistants, RAG data fetches, and edge-to-cloud inference paths. Use application, SLA class, site, and color filters to determine whether SD-WAN path quality changed during the incident.

charts.name: App-Route Latency
charts.description: Value: shows SD-WAN application-aware routing latency. Interpretation: rising latency by application, site, or color indicates a degraded path for SaaS, custom app, or AI/model traffic.

charts.name: App-Route Jitter
charts.description: Value: shows SD-WAN application-aware routing jitter. Interpretation: jitter spikes indicate unstable WAN paths for latency-sensitive applications and model/API calls.

charts.name: App-Route Loss
charts.description: Value: shows SD-WAN application-aware routing loss. Interpretation: non-zero or rising loss explains retransmits, failed API calls, poor SaaS experience, or model endpoint errors.

charts.name: App SLA Status
charts.description: Value: shows encoded SD-WAN app-route SLA state. Interpretation: degraded or failed SLA rows show which app, class, site, or color violated policy.

dashboards.name: 04 Interfaces Circuits Cellular And Capacity
dashboards.description: WAN/service interface, circuit, cellular, and capacity dashboard for SD-WAN incidents.
dashboards.value: Correlates WAN/service interface state, traffic, errors, drops, circuit pressure, and cellular/failover evidence around an incident window.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to correlate dataplane symptoms and change evidence. Interpretation: read interface state/traffic/errors/drops beside alarm, event, and audit counts to determine whether physical/circuit symptoms or recent changes explain the incident.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page ties SD-WAN interface and transport symptoms to event evidence. Use it when a site, application, or color is already suspected and you need to line up interface state, traffic silence or surge, errors, drops, alarms, events, and audit/config changes.

charts.name: Interface Status
charts.description: Value: shows WAN and service interface operational state. Interpretation: admin-up but operational-down rows usually indicate circuit, cable, provider, or failover impact.

charts.name: Interface Traffic
charts.description: Value: shows interface receive/transmit traffic volume from SD-WAN Manager. Interpretation: sudden silence, surge, or asymmetry around the incident points to circuit/path or application shift.

charts.name: Interface Errors And Drops
charts.description: Value: shows SD-WAN interface errors and packet drops. Interpretation: new or sustained growth on WAN paths explains app-route loss, failover, or degraded application experience.

charts.name: Alarms Events And Audit Counts
charts.description: Value: summarizes SD-WAN alarm, event, and audit evidence by type, severity, status, site, and policy. Interpretation: spikes during the incident window show control-plane, policy, security, deployment, or operator-change evidence to review in logs.

dashboards.name: 05 Policy QoS Security And Service Edge
dashboards.description: Policy, QoS, security, SIG/SSE/Umbrella, firewall, IPS, URL filtering, and service-edge coverage dashboard.
dashboards.value: Shows whether policy, QoS, and security/service-edge opt-in groups are producing evidence or exposing feature/license/API gaps.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to use policy, QoS, and security/service-edge coverage during an incident. Interpretation: use object counts and unavailable/skipped charts to confirm whether drops or service insertion evidence is available for the affected path.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page is for SD-WAN policy and security incident evidence. Enable `policy_qos` and `security` when investigating strict SLA drops, ACL/policy drops, QoS queue pressure, SIG/SSE/Umbrella tunnels, ZBFW/UTD/IPS, URL filtering, or inspection-related detours.

charts.name: Policy And QoS Objects
charts.description: Value: shows object counts from the policy and QoS feature group. Interpretation: zero or missing counts during an investigation usually means the group is disabled, unsupported, or unavailable through the current role/version.

charts.name: Security And Service Edge Objects
charts.description: Value: shows object counts from SD-WAN security and service-edge feature groups. Interpretation: use this to confirm whether SIG, SSE, Umbrella, firewall, IPS, or URL-filtering evidence exists for the incident window.

charts.name: Policy Security Coverage Gaps
charts.description: Value: shows policy/security feature endpoints that were unavailable or skipped. Interpretation: gaps usually indicate license, deployment, version, permission, or missing target scope rather than healthy policy/security state.
charts.signalflow: data('sdwan.service.unavailable', filter=filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'policy_qos') or filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'security')).sum(by=['sdwan.collection.group', 'sdwan.collection.operation']).publish(label='Unavailable'); data('sdwan.service.skipped', filter=filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'policy_qos') or filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'security')).sum(by=['sdwan.collection.group', 'sdwan.skip.reason']).publish(label='Skipped')

charts.name: Policy Security Resource Status
charts.description: Value: shows health state for policy, QoS, security, and service-edge objects. Interpretation: degraded or failed statuses identify product modules that can change routing, security, or application treatment. Interpretation: list rows encode SD-WAN resource status by collection group, operation, site, and status.

dashboards.name: 06 AppQoE Optimization And Flow Evidence
dashboards.description: AppQoE, DRE, TCP optimization, SSL proxy, and flow evidence dashboard.
dashboards.value: Shows AppQoE and flow opt-in coverage so operators can correlate optimization behavior with app-route symptoms.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how optimization and flow evidence complements app-route metrics. Interpretation: enable AppQoE and flow groups when app-route quality changed but operators need DRE/TCP/SSL proxy or DPI/cflowd context.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page covers SD-WAN optimization and flow evidence. Enable `appqoe` and `flows` when you need to know whether DRE, TCP optimization, SSL proxy, app-flow, DPI, or cflowd evidence explains an application incident.

charts.name: AppQoE Objects
charts.description: Value: shows AppQoE, DRE, and optimization object counts. Interpretation: object counts indicate the feature group is returning evidence; unavailable endpoints indicate feature or API coverage gaps.

charts.name: Flow Objects
charts.description: Value: shows bounded flow/DPI/cflowd object counts. Interpretation: use counts for evidence coverage and keep raw flow cardinality in logs or downstream flow tooling.

charts.name: AppQoE And Flow Resource Status
charts.description: Value: shows health state for AppQoE and flow evidence objects. Interpretation: degraded statuses explain why optimization or flow attribution may not match user experience. Interpretation: list rows encode SD-WAN resource status by collection group, operation, site, and status.

dashboards.name: 07 Cloud OnRamp Multicloud Colocation And Gateways
dashboards.description: Cloud OnRamp SaaS, custom app, multicloud, interconnect, colocation, and gateway coverage dashboard.
dashboards.value: Shows Cloud OnRamp and cloud gateway evidence for SaaS, custom app, multicloud, colocation, and AI cloud path incidents.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how Cloud OnRamp evidence fits into WAN and AI/cloud troubleshooting. Interpretation: compare Cloud OnRamp coverage with app-route quality and feature gaps when SaaS, model API, or cloud gateway paths degrade.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page tracks SD-WAN cloud and gateway evidence. Enable `cloud_onramp` to correlate SaaS/custom application vQoE, DIA/gateway state, cloud provider, multicloud, colocation, and interconnect evidence with app-route path metrics.

charts.name: Cloud OnRamp Objects
charts.description: Value: shows Cloud OnRamp object counts by operation. Interpretation: use object count changes to identify SaaS/custom app or cloud gateway state changes during incidents.

charts.name: Cloud OnRamp Coverage Gaps
charts.description: Value: shows unavailable Cloud OnRamp endpoint families. Interpretation: unavailable endpoints often indicate a feature, license, cloud provider, version, or permission gap.

charts.name: Cloud OnRamp Resource Status
charts.description: Value: shows health state for Cloud OnRamp and cloud-services objects. Interpretation: degraded rows identify cloud gateway or SaaS handoff risk rather than branch transport failure. Interpretation: list rows encode SD-WAN resource status by collection group, operation, site, and status.

dashboards.name: 08 Routing Branch Services And SD-Routing
dashboards.description: Routing services, branch services, SD-Branch, and SD-Routing coverage dashboard.
dashboards.value: Shows routing, WLAN, voice, NFV/service-hosting, and SD-Routing evidence that can explain branch or service-side incidents.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how service-side routing and branch services are represented. Interpretation: enable routing and branch service groups when app impact may be caused by VPN/VRF routing, branch WLAN/voice, NFV, or autonomous SD-Routing devices.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page covers branch and service-side evidence beyond the SD-WAN overlay: BGP, OSPF, EIGRP, OMP detail, routes/FIB, NAT, DHCP, VRRP, multicast, NTP, WLAN, voice, UCSE, VM lifecycle, NFV, SD-Branch, and SD-Routing/autonomous routers.

charts.name: Routing Service Objects
charts.description: Value: shows routing-service object counts from opt-in collection. Interpretation: changes or gaps help determine whether service-side routing data is available for the affected VPN or site.

charts.name: Branch Service Objects
charts.description: Value: shows branch-service object counts from opt-in collection. Interpretation: use this for WLAN, voice, UCSE, VM, NFV, and SD-Branch evidence availability.

charts.name: Routing And Branch Resource Status
charts.description: Value: shows health state for routing and branch-service objects. Interpretation: degraded rows point to BGP, routes, WLAN, voice, or branch service ownership. Interpretation: list rows encode SD-WAN resource status by collection group, operation, site, and status.

dashboards.name: 09 Lifecycle Advisories Energy And Hardware
dashboards.description: Lifecycle, compliance, advisory, reboot/crash, hardware, power, and energy coverage dashboard.
dashboards.value: Correlates device lifecycle, compliance, crash/reboot, certificate, advisory, EoX, hardware, power, and energy evidence with incidents.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how lifecycle and hardware evidence can explain SD-WAN symptoms. Interpretation: use this page when incidents may be caused by certificate validity, reboot/crash, advisories, EoX, maintenance, environment, SFP, power, thermal, or energy issues.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page combines lifecycle/compliance and hardware/energy evidence. Enable `lifecycle_compliance` and `hardware_energy` to correlate certificate lifecycle, software inventory, advisories, EoX/EoS, reboots, crash logs, power, thermal, fan, SFP, and energy data.

charts.name: Lifecycle Compliance Objects
charts.description: Value: shows lifecycle/compliance object counts. Interpretation: count changes or unavailable endpoints reveal whether reboot/crash/advisory/compliance evidence is available.

charts.name: Hardware Energy Objects
charts.description: Value: shows hardware and energy object counts. Interpretation: use this to confirm whether environment, SFP, power, thermal, and energy evidence exists for affected devices.

charts.name: Lifecycle Hardware Resource Status
charts.description: Value: shows health state for lifecycle, compliance, hardware, and energy objects. Interpretation: degraded rows indicate device stability, crash, reboot, environment, or power risk. Interpretation: list rows encode SD-WAN resource status by collection group, operation, site, and status.

dashboards.name: 10 Alarms Events Audit And Change Evidence
dashboards.description: Alarm, event, audit, management security, and hardening evidence dashboard.
dashboards.value: Shows active/recent alarms, events, audit records, user/session evidence, and hardening-relevant management-plane changes.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to use logs and event counts during SD-WAN incident autopsy. Interpretation: line up alarm/event/audit spikes with app, overlay, interface, policy, or security symptoms.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page is the SD-WAN change and evidence queue. Use event counts with SD-WAN logs to review alarms, audit/config changes, policy deployments, unauthorized login activity, active sessions, validity/certificate changes, and hardening-relevant management-plane events.

charts.name: Alarms Events Audit Counts
charts.description: Value: summarizes SD-WAN alarm, event, and audit evidence by type, severity, status, site, and policy. Interpretation: spikes show when to pivot into SD-WAN logs for original event bodies.

charts.name: Management Security Objects
charts.description: Value: shows management-security object counts when the opt-in group is enabled. Interpretation: use this for user/session and hardening evidence availability.

charts.name: Management Security Resource Status
charts.description: Value: shows health state for management security and active session evidence. Interpretation: degraded rows or unusual counts can explain operational access, auth, or administrative risk during incidents. Interpretation: list rows encode SD-WAN resource status by collection group, operation, site, and status.

dashboards.name: 11 Network-Wide Path Insight And Incident Readout
dashboards.description: Network-Wide Path Insight, ThousandEyes agent status, and deep incident readout dashboard.
dashboards.value: Shows NWPI read-only result coverage and ThousandEyes agent correlation for deep SD-WAN path investigations.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how NWPI and ThousandEyes agent evidence supports deep incident readout. Interpretation: use this page after app-route or interface symptoms identify a path that needs hop, QoS, SLA, anti-replay, security, or external-agent context.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page is for deep SD-WAN incident readout. Enable `nwpi` for read-only Network-Wide Path Insight task/event/result coverage and `thousandeyes` for SD-WAN Manager-visible ThousandEyes agent status or correlation. Direct ThousandEyes test telemetry remains outside this receiver.

charts.name: NWPI Objects
charts.description: Value: shows Network-Wide Path Insight object counts. Interpretation: counts indicate read-only NWPI evidence exists for SLA, QoS, WAN loss, security alert, anti-replay, hop, or app readout analysis.

charts.name: ThousandEyes Agent Objects
charts.description: Value: shows SD-WAN Manager-visible ThousandEyes agent object counts. Interpretation: use this to confirm agent deployment/status evidence is available before correlating with direct ThousandEyes telemetry.

charts.name: NWPI And ThousandEyes Resource Status
charts.description: Value: shows health state for network-wide path insight and ThousandEyes agent objects. Interpretation: degraded rows identify missing synthetic/user-path evidence rather than true absence of path issues. Interpretation: list rows encode SD-WAN resource status by collection group, operation, site, and status.

dashboards.name: 12 Service Desk End User Impact Triage
dashboards.description: Service-desk-first dashboard for user-visible SD-WAN impact by site, application, SLA class, and likely symptom.
dashboards.value: Answers which users, sites, and applications are likely affected before exposing operators to SD-WAN implementation detail.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: gives service desk and incident coordinators an end-user-first SD-WAN view. Interpretation: start here when tickets say users cannot reach SaaS, AI assistants, model APIs, internal apps, voice, or branch services; escalate with the site, app, SLA class, and symptom already identified.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page is intentionally end-user-first. It turns SD-WAN telemetry into service-desk questions: which sites are affected, which applications or AI/model endpoints are degraded, whether the symptom looks like loss, latency, jitter, outage, interface/circuit failure, or recent change, and whether the SD-WAN Manager data itself is trustworthy.

charts.name: Sites With User-Visible Risk
charts.description: Value: shows sites where users may be affected because device, overlay, BFD, or interface state is degraded. Interpretation: rows with down or degraded status are the first sites to validate with user tickets and synthetic checks.
charts.signalflow: data('cisco.device.up', filter=filter('cisco.controller.type', 'sdwan_manager')).mean(by=['sdwan.site.id', 'host.name', 'sdwan.system_ip']).publish(label='Device up'); data('sdwan.bfd.session.status').mean(by=['sdwan.site.id', 'host.name', 'sdwan.local.color', 'sdwan.remote.color', 'sdwan.status']).publish(label='BFD status'); data('system.network.interface.status', filter=filter('cisco.controller.type', 'sdwan_manager')).mean(by=['sdwan.site.id', 'host.name', 'network.interface.name', 'sdwan.tloc.color']).publish(label='Interface status')

charts.name: Applications With SLA Risk
charts.description: Value: shows applications and SLA classes with degraded SD-WAN app-route state. Interpretation: degraded rows identify what users are likely complaining about and which SLA class or transport color is involved.

charts.name: User Symptom Classifier
charts.description: Value: groups likely user symptoms into loss, latency, jitter, interface drops, and interface errors. Interpretation: compare the largest or newest signal during the ticket window to decide whether to route the incident to WAN, provider, policy/security, or application teams.

charts.name: Recent Change Or Alarm Evidence
charts.description: Value: shows alarms, events, and audit records near the user-impact window. Interpretation: spikes around ticket creation suggest a network change, policy deployment, security event, device event, or controller-side alarm may explain the user reports.

charts.name: Can We Trust This User Impact View
charts.description: Value: shows whether SD-WAN Manager collection is healthy enough for service desk triage. Interpretation: partial scrape, API errors, unavailable groups, or skipped groups mean the user-impact view may be incomplete.

dashboards.name: 13 Branch And Remote Site Experience
dashboards.description: Branch-experience dashboard for site health, WAN transports, failover, capacity, BFD path stability, and local service impact.
dashboards.value: Shows whether a branch or remote site is having a user experience problem caused by transport, circuit, failover, interface, or overlay instability.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: gives branch operations and field teams a site-first SD-WAN experience page. Interpretation: use this when a location reports broad slowness, intermittent SaaS, voice quality, payment system failure, guest Wi-Fi issues, or branch outage symptoms.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page is for branch and remote-site experience. It keeps site availability, WAN Edge reachability, BFD/TLOC path health, interface/circuit state, drops/errors, and branch-service coverage together so operations teams can quickly tell whether the user impact is local site, provider, transport color, or overlay related.

charts.name: WAN Edge Availability By Site
charts.description: Value: shows WAN Edge device availability by site. Interpretation: down devices usually mean broad branch impact or loss of SD-WAN visibility at that location.

charts.name: Transport Color Health By Site
charts.description: Value: shows BFD path state by site and transport color. Interpretation: a single degraded color points to provider/circuit impact; multiple degraded colors suggest site, device, or controller-side impact.

charts.name: Circuit Traffic Errors And Drops
charts.description: Value: shows circuit/interface traffic, errors, and drops by site and color. Interpretation: traffic silence, spikes, errors, or drops explain branch slowness, app timeouts, or failover.
charts.signalflow: data('system.network.io', filter=filter('cisco.controller.type', 'sdwan_manager')).rate().sum(by=['sdwan.site.id', 'network.interface.name', 'sdwan.tloc.color', 'network.io.direction']).publish(label='Traffic bytes/sec'); data('system.network.errors', filter=filter('cisco.controller.type', 'sdwan_manager')).rate().sum(by=['sdwan.site.id', 'network.interface.name', 'sdwan.tloc.color']).publish(label='Errors/sec'); data('system.network.packet.dropped', filter=filter('cisco.controller.type', 'sdwan_manager')).rate().sum(by=['sdwan.site.id', 'network.interface.name', 'sdwan.tloc.color']).publish(label='Drops/sec')

charts.name: Branch Services Coverage
charts.description: Value: shows whether branch-service opt-in data exists for WLAN, voice, UCSE, VM, NFV, and SD-Branch investigations. Interpretation: missing or unavailable data means branch-service experience requires enabling the group or using another source.
charts.signalflow: data('sdwan.collection.object.count', filter=filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'branch_services')).sum(by=['sdwan.collection.operation', 'sdwan.status']).publish(label='Branch service objects'); data('sdwan.service.unavailable', filter=filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'branch_services')).sum(by=['sdwan.collection.operation']).publish(label='Unavailable')

dashboards.name: 14 SaaS AI And Critical Application Experience
dashboards.description: Application-owner dashboard for SaaS, AI/model API, RAG, edge-to-cloud inference, and other critical application paths.
dashboards.value: Shows application experience by app, site, SLA class, color, Cloud OnRamp coverage, AppQoE coverage, and security/service-edge evidence.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: gives application owners a path-quality view for SaaS, AI assistants, model APIs, RAG data fetches, and critical business apps. Interpretation: use app, site, SLA class, and color filters to determine whether SD-WAN is contributing to user-facing application errors.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page is for application and AI service owners. It answers whether a critical app, SaaS service, model API, RAG data path, or edge-to-cloud inference flow is seeing SD-WAN loss, latency, jitter, SLA violation, Cloud OnRamp path issues, AppQoE/optimization behavior, or security/service-edge detours.

charts.name: Application Path Quality
charts.description: Value: shows latency, jitter, and loss by application, site, SLA class, and color. Interpretation: path quality degradation points to WAN or SD-WAN path contribution to user-visible application errors.

charts.name: Critical App SLA State
charts.description: Value: shows app-route SLA state for critical apps. Interpretation: degraded status by app and SLA class gives application owners a direct SD-WAN policy signal to correlate with app errors.

charts.name: Cloud OnRamp And AppQoE Evidence
charts.description: Value: shows whether Cloud OnRamp and AppQoE opt-in groups are producing application-path evidence. Interpretation: use this when SaaS/AI experience depends on DIA gateways, best-path selection, DRE, TCP optimization, or SSL proxy behavior.

charts.name: Security Or Policy Detour Evidence
charts.description: Value: shows whether policy/QoS and security/service-edge groups are producing evidence for the app path. Interpretation: object counts or gaps help decide whether inspection, SSE/SIG, Umbrella, firewall, IPS, QoS, or policy enforcement may explain app degradation.
charts.signalflow: data('sdwan.collection.object.count', filter=filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'policy_qos')).sum(by=['sdwan.collection.operation', 'sdwan.status']).publish(label='Policy QoS'); data('sdwan.collection.object.count', filter=filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'security')).sum(by=['sdwan.collection.operation', 'sdwan.status']).publish(label='Security'); data('sdwan.service.unavailable', filter=filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'policy_qos') or filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'security')).sum(by=['sdwan.collection.group', 'sdwan.collection.operation']).publish(label='Unavailable')

charts.name: Critical App Resource Status
charts.description: Value: shows app, cloud, policy, and security object health for critical applications. Interpretation: degraded rows identify whether user impact likely belongs to cloud handoff, optimization, policy, or security treatment. Interpretation: list rows encode SD-WAN resource status by collection group, operation, site, and status.
charts.signalflow: data('sdwan.resource.status', filter=filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'cloud_onramp') or filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'appqoe') or filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'policy_qos') or filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'security')).mean(by=['sdwan.collection.group', 'sdwan.collection.operation', 'sdwan.site.id', 'sdwan.status']).publish(label='Resource status')

dashboards.name: 15 Incident Commander User Impact Summary
dashboards.description: Incident-command dashboard for stakeholder updates about affected sites, apps, symptom direction, data trust, and likely owning team.
dashboards.value: Summarizes user-facing SD-WAN impact in language useful for incident commanders, service owners, and leadership updates.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: gives incident commanders a concise stakeholder view of SD-WAN user impact. Interpretation: use this page to prepare updates: affected sites, affected apps, symptom type, visibility confidence, and whether ownership points to WAN/provider, SD-WAN overlay, policy/security, or application/cloud.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page is not for deep packet-path diagnosis. It is for incident command: what is affected, how users feel it, whether SD-WAN telemetry is trustworthy, what changed recently, and which team is most likely to own the next action.

charts.name: Affected Sites Summary
charts.description: Value: lists sites with device, interface, BFD, or SLA degradation. Interpretation: these are the sites to name in stakeholder updates and validate against tickets or synthetic monitors.

charts.name: Affected Applications Summary
charts.description: Value: summarizes degraded application path quality by app and SLA class. Interpretation: use this to name affected services and whether symptoms are likely latency, jitter, loss, or SLA state.

charts.name: Likely Owning Team Signals
charts.description: Value: groups evidence by WAN/interface, overlay/BFD, policy/security, application optimization, and recent change. Interpretation: the strongest signal helps route the bridge to provider/WAN, SD-WAN, security, application, or change owner.
charts.signalflow: data('system.network.packet.dropped', filter=filter('cisco.controller.type', 'sdwan_manager')).rate().sum(by=['sdwan.site.id']).publish(label='WAN drops/sec'); data('sdwan.bfd.session.status').mean(by=['sdwan.site.id', 'sdwan.status']).publish(label='Overlay'); data('sdwan.collection.object.count', filter=filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'policy_qos') or filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'security')).sum(by=['sdwan.collection.group']).publish(label='Policy security'); data('sdwan.collection.object.count', filter=filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'appqoe') or filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'cloud_onramp')).sum(by=['sdwan.collection.group']).publish(label='App cloud'); data('sdwan.event.count').sum(by=['sdwan.event.type', 'sdwan.severity']).publish(label='Change events')

charts.name: Visibility Confidence
charts.description: Value: shows whether SD-WAN data is complete enough for stakeholder updates. Interpretation: partial scrape, API errors, unavailable groups, or skipped target groups should be disclosed as confidence limits.

charts.name: Incident Visibility Trust
charts.description: Value: shows whether critical incident evidence families are healthy enough to trust. Interpretation: unhealthy rows mean the incident commander should call out visibility gaps while assigning ownership. Interpretation: list rows encode SD-WAN resource status by collection group, operation, site, and status.
charts.signalflow: data('sdwan.resource.status', filter=filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'cloud_onramp') or filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'appqoe') or filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'policy_qos') or filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'security') or filter('sdwan.collection.group', 'nwpi')).mean(by=['sdwan.collection.group', 'sdwan.collection.operation', 'sdwan.site.id', 'sdwan.status']).publish(label='Resource status')
